chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man who bought an estate, and he had been entering it and leaving it. Then when he paid the money, he went to the estate and inspected it, then returned and asked the owner to revoke the sale, but he did not revoke it for him. So Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “If he had turned it over and looked at ninety-nine parts of it, then one part remained that he had not seen, he would still have, in that case, the option of inspection.”

key_terms.خِيَارُ الرُّؤْيَةِ: the buyer's legal option due to not having seen the entirety of the item
key_terms.ضَيْعَةً: an estate or landed property being purchased
key_terms.فَاسْتَقَالَ: he requested that the sale be annulled
key_terms.فَفَتَّشَهَا: he inspected and examined it carefully
key_terms.قِطْعَةٌ: a part or section of the property

ai.seo_question: Does a buyer still have the option to cancel a sale if part of the property was not seen?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes a legal ruling concerning khiyār al-ruʾyah, the option arising from incomplete inspection in a sale. It indicates that if any portion of the purchased property remained unseen, the buyer retains the right to rescind based on that unseen part.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3976 - Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrates from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:

I asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about a man who purchased a property. He used to enter and leave it, but after paying the price and inspecting the property, he returned and requested the seller to annul the sale, but the seller refused.
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), said: "Even if he had examined and inspected ninety-nine parts of it, and one part remained unseen, he would still have the right of option (Khiyar al-Ru'yah) based on inspection."
